headline: IonQ, a quantum computing company, has closed its roughly $2 billion sale of shares and warrants at $40 a unit, including warrants for 100 million more shares at $69.46, a US securities filing shows.
score_reason: Pool score kept: it completes a deal we carried on 15 Oct 2026, with the final terms as the only new facts.
importance_line: Current IonQ shareholders could see their stake diluted if the 100 million warrants are used, which pays off only if the share price rises above $69.46, and the company says the money is for its quantum computing, networking, sensing and security business.
summary: IonQ said in a US Securities and Exchange Commission filing of 16 Oct 2026, relayed by TradingView, that it sold 20.5 million shares and 29.5 million pre-funded warrants (warrants to buy shares later for a nominal $0.0001 each) at $40 per unit, each coming with two Series C warrants, 100 million in all, to buy shares at $69.46 within seven years. In our 15 Oct 2026 edition we carried the roughly $2 billion pricing announced on 14 Oct 2026; the new fact is that AWP Alliance News, summarising the filing, reports the offering closed on 16 Oct 2026, with all the warrants usable immediately.
notes: The url is the SEC filing index named in the AWP Alliance News brief; the filing itself (HTTP 403) and Stock Titan (403) could not be opened. Text was read on TradingView (two sentences), the AWP brief on vermoegenszentrum.ch and Quantum Computing Report. Default category RES kept; MKT would also fit as a company financing.
